Estimation

Source: vignettes/estimators.Rmd
estimators.Rmd

This page describes how the package runs the paper’s 2x2 comparisons, then writes out every estimator it returns and the influence function its standard error is built from. Notation follows Notation and output. Section, theorem and appendix numbers refer to Leventer (2025), Identification of Child Penalties; appendices are referred to by name, because their letters differ between the arXiv and journal versions: Estimation appendix is the appendix on estimation and inference, Proportional appendix the online appendix on proportional DID and TD. Formulas that are not in the paper are marked not in the paper.

Running the comparisons

multiple_treatment_group_analysis() runs the grid of 2x2 comparisons that the paper’s figures use. For each treatment group dd in treatment_groups and event time e=0,…,He = 0, \dots, H (periods_post = H), the target age is a=d+ea = d + e and the control group is the closest not-yet-treated group, d′=a+1d' = a + 1 (Section 1.3). Pre-treatment event times e=−(pre+K),…,−(pre+1)e = -(\text{pre} + K), \dots, -(\text{pre} + 1) (periods_pre = K) are estimated against every control group used after treatment, d′=d+1,…,d+H+1d' = d + 1, \dots, d + H + 1: the identifying assumptions are about each treatment-control pair, so each pair has its own validation test (Section 2.3). The column control_offset =d′−d= d' - d identifies the pair. max_control_group is the largest age at first birth used as a control (the paper’s DmaxD_{max}). single_treatment_group_analysis() runs one comparison.

res <- multiple_treatment_group_analysis(data, treatment_groups = 24:34,
                                         periods_post = 5, periods_pre = 3,
                                         max_control_group = 40)

With the paper’s sample this grid is the one behind its figures: treatment groups 24 to 34, event times 0 to 5, pre-treatment event times −4-4 to −2-2 (baseline d−1d - 1), and controls up to 40 (Replicating the paper).

Input data. data is a data.frame or data.table in long format, one row per person and age; the panel need not be balanced. The columns are located by name:

argument default content
id_name "id" person identifier (the clustering unit)
age_name "age" age, numeric
D_name "D" age at first birth, constant within person; a missing (or infinite) value means the person never has a child
female_name "female" gender, constant within person; 1 / TRUE is female and 0 / FALSE male; labels such as "female" / "male", "f" / "m", "woman" / "man" are also accepted
Y_name "Y" earnings, numeric; zeros are allowed, while the ratio rows need positive cell means

Rows with a missing outcome are dropped with a message. The functions stop with an error if a person-age pair is repeated, if female or D varies within a person, if a gender label is not recognised, or if only one gender is present. data is not modified. Persons with a missing D stay in the data, belong to no treatment or control group, and count in the totals the standard errors are scaled by.

Setup

Data are one row per person ii and age tt, with earnings YY, gender g∈{f,m}g \in \{f, m\} and age at first birth DD. A 2x2 comparison has a treatment group dd, a control group d′>ad' > a, a target age aa and a baseline age b=d−preb = d - \text{pre} (default b=d−1b = d - 1).

Cell means. For a cell (g,k,t)(g, k, t), with indicator Sit=1{Gi=g,Di=k,age=t}S_{it} = 1\{G_i = g, D_i = k, \text{age} = t\}, μ̂(g,k,t)=∑i,t′Sit′Yit′∑i,t′Sit′,ψμ(g,k,t)=SP̂(S)(Y−μ̂(g,k,t)), \hat\mu(g,k,t) = \frac{\sum_{i,t'} S_{it'} Y_{it'}}{\sum_{i,t'} S_{it'}}, \qquad \psi_{\mu(g,k,t)} = \frac{S}{\hat P(S)}\,\big(Y - \hat\mu(g,k,t)\big), where P̂(S)\hat P(S) is the share of person-age rows in the cell (Estimation appendix). Every estimator below is a smooth function of eight cell means, μ1=μ(g,d,b),μ2=μ(g,d′,a),μ3=μ(g,d′,b),μ4=μ(g,d,a),g∈{f,m}, \mu_1 = \mu(g,d,b),\quad \mu_2 = \mu(g,d',a),\quad \mu_3 = \mu(g,d',b),\quad \mu_4 = \mu(g,d,a), \qquad g \in \{f, m\}, and its influence function ψ\psi follows from theirs by the chain rule.

Standard errors. For an estimator with influence function ψ\psi, with nn person-age rows, GG persons and clusters cc = persons, Var̂=1n2∑c(∑i∈cψi)2GG−1. \widehat{\mathrm{Var}} = \frac{1}{n^2}\sum_{c}\Big(\sum_{i \in c}\psi_i\Big)^2\,\frac{G}{G-1}. Confidence intervals are est±1.96se\text{est} \pm 1.96\,\text{se}.

Rows of single_treatment_group_analysis()

Imputations of counterfactual earnings. Additive (DID) and multiplicative: δ̂APO(g)=μ1+μ2−μ3,ψδAPO(g)=ψ1+ψ2−ψ3; \hat\delta_{APO}(g) = \mu_1 + \mu_2 - \mu_3, \qquad \psi_{\delta_{APO}(g)} = \psi_1 + \psi_2 - \psi_3; δ̂APO×(g)=μ1μ2μ3,ψδAPO×(g)=δ̂APO×(g)(ψ1μ1+ψ2μ2−ψ3μ3). \hat\delta^{\times}_{APO}(g) = \frac{\mu_1\,\mu_2}{\mu_3}, \qquad \psi_{\delta^{\times}_{APO}(g)} = \hat\delta^{\times}_{APO}(g)\Big(\frac{\psi_1}{\mu_1} + \frac{\psi_2}{\mu_2} - \frac{\psi_3}{\mu_3}\Big).

NA (no anticipation), DID-PT (parallel trends), TD-PT and NTD-PT are the assumptions of Sections 2 and 3 of the paper; TD-E-LOGS and TD-PR are those of the Proportional appendix. For TD_E_LOGS the counterfactual ratio uses δ̂APO×\hat\delta^{\times}_{APO}; the share_parenthood row of TD_E_LOGS uses ρ̂cf×\hat\rho^{\times}_{cf} in place of ρ̂cf\hat\rho_{cf}.

Rows behind the paper’s figures. Pre-treatment DID_Female / DID_Male ATE rows: the DID validation tests (Figure 3). Conventional gap_theta: the conventional estimator (Figure 6b), its pre-treatment rows the NTD validation tests (Figure 5), and with bias_bounds() the bias-bounding exercise (Figure 4). NTD rho_obs and rho_cf: the two ratios (Figure 6a); NTD rho_effect: the new estimator (Figure 6b); the two ratios, or share_parenthood and share_other, give the accounting (Figure 6c). TD_E_LOGS and TD_PR: the Proportional appendix’s validation and estimate figures. Aggregates: Aggregation. Each figure is reproduced on simulated data in Replicating the paper.

Accounting (standard errors not in the paper). The paper splits the observed gender gap 1−ρ(d)1 - \rho(d) into parenthood, ρ(∞)−ρ(d)\rho(\infty) - \rho(d), and other factors, 1−ρ(∞)1 - \rho(\infty), and reports parenthood’s share (Section 4.2) as a point estimate. The package also reports its standard error, from the influence function above. Derivation: write s=N/Ms = N/M with N=ρcf−ρobsN = \rho_{cf} - \rho_{obs} and M=1−ρobsM = 1 - \rho_{obs}; then ψs=ψN/M−NψM/M2\psi_s = \psi_N/M - N\psi_M/M^2, with ψN=ψρcf−ψρobs\psi_N = \psi_{\rho_{cf}} - \psi_{\rho_{obs}} and ψM=−ψρobs\psi_M = -\psi_{\rho_{obs}}, which gives the formula in the table.

bias_bounds()

The bias-corrected conventional gap at an assumed fathers’ effect θ(m)\theta(m) (Proposition 2, in the form of the Estimation appendix), with Δ̂\hat\Delta the NTD rho_effect estimate: B̂(θ(m))=Δ̂δ̂APO(m)δ̂APO(f)(1+θ(m)), \hat B(\theta(m)) = \hat\Delta\,\frac{\hat\delta_{APO}(m)}{\hat\delta_{APO}(f)}\,\big(1 + \theta(m)\big), ψB=(1+θ(m))[δAPO(m)δAPO(f)ψΔ+ΔδAPO(f)ψδAPO(m)−ΔδAPO(m)δAPO(f)2ψδAPO(f)]. \psi_{B} = \big(1 + \theta(m)\big)\Big[\frac{\delta_{APO}(m)}{\delta_{APO}(f)}\psi_{\Delta} + \frac{\Delta}{\delta_{APO}(f)}\psi_{\delta_{APO}(m)} - \frac{\Delta\,\delta_{APO}(m)}{\delta_{APO}(f)^2}\psi_{\delta_{APO}(f)}\Big]. The estimator is in the paper; its influence function is not in the paper. The standard error scales with 1+θ(m)1 + \theta(m).

aggregate_estimands()

For event time ee, the treatment groups 𝒟(e)\mathcal D(e) with an estimate, group estimates BdB_d and group shares pdp_d (within gender for DID_Female / DID_Male, across genders otherwise), Pe=∑d∈𝒟(e)pdP_e = \sum_{d \in \mathcal D(e)} p_d and wd=pd/Pew_d = p_d / P_e:

  • weighted_avg: Â(e)=∑dwdB̂d\hat A(e) = \sum_d w_d \hat B_d, with (Estimation appendix, aggregate estimator) ψA(e)=1Pe∑d∈𝒟(e)[(Bd−A(e))ψpd+pdψBd],ψpd=1{D=d}−pd \psi_{A(e)} = \frac{1}{P_e}\sum_{d \in \mathcal D(e)}\Big[(B_d - A(e))\,\psi_{p_d} + p_d\,\psi_{B_d}\Big], \qquad \psi_{p_d} = 1\{D = d\} - p_d (1{G=g,D=d}−pg,d1\{G = g, D = d\} - p_{g,d} for within-gender shares). With fixed or uniform weights the first term drops out. For share_other the influence function is minus that of share_parenthood.
  • ratio_of_avgs (DID_Female, DID_Male): θ̂Agg,2=num/den\hat\theta_{Agg,2} = num/den with num=∑dwdδ̂ATE,dnum = \sum_d w_d \hat\delta_{ATE,d} and den=∑dwdδ̂APO,dden = \sum_d w_d \hat\delta_{APO,d}, and influence function ψnum/den−numψden/den2\psi_{num}/den - num\,\psi_{den}/den^2, where ψnum\psi_{num} and ψden\psi_{den} are the influence functions of the two weighted averages above (each with its share term).

Pre-treatment event times have one cell per control group; include_pre = TRUE aggregates each control offset d′−dd' - d separately. The share term is put on the person-age scale with the average number of ages per person, which is exact for a balanced panel.

Group influence functions are summed per person across treatment groups before squaring, so the standard errors account for persons who are controls for several treatment groups.

Standard errors checked against a person-level (cluster) bootstrap in tests/testthat/: TD_E_LOGS and TD_PR rho_effect / gap_theta_pre, NTD share_parenthood, and bias_bounds(). TD_E_LOGS and TD_PR are also checked by Monte Carlo (dev/sims/td_sim_results.md in the source repository).
